svg.text: CBIS-DDSM — Breast Lesion Segmentation: Project Map
Segmenting cancerous tissue on screening mammography · dataset composition, radiology metrics, model landscape, planned pipeline · MLB 2026–2027
Grounded in Lee et al., Scientific Data 4:170177 (2017) · the TCIA CBIS-DDSM collection record · Shen et al., Scientific Reports 9:12495 (2019). Nothing here is built yet.

a real improvement — but still not expert-grade
example ROIs from the paper; dense breasts are exactly

What this means for the project
Labels are silver, not gold — treat 0.79 as the
masses first, add calcifications as a stretch goal
Always report Dice split by density and subtlety —

svg.text: fall out of it and give you

g.text: input = full mammogram or ROI-cropped patch
output = mask, comparable to the provided ROI
CADx (diagnosis): is it benign or malignant?
both obtained by aggregating the pixel map
CADe is limited by false positives; CADx is not yet clinically approved
full image (~3000 × 5000 px) vs patches vs multi-scale
single view vs CC + MLO fusion per breast
Dice / F1 — the primary number (used by Lee 2017)
Hausdorff-95, ASSD — boundary error in mm
Mass margin and shape are themselves diagnostic:
a boundary metric is not cosmetic here.
PPV · NPV — depend on prevalence, state it
ROC-AUC, written Az in the older CAD papers
FROC curve & FPPI — false positives per image
Anchors: CADe 81–98% sens. at 0.2–3.2 FPPI; CADx Az 0.77–0.94
These are free axes for the results slides: performance
vs difficulty is far more convincing than one mean.
Metric trap — pixel accuracy is meaningless on this data.

A lesion covers under 1% of a mammogram, so predicting all-background scores > 99%. Use Dice and AUC-PR, and pair every operating point with its FPPI: a CADe system is judged on how many false marks must be dismissed per image.
Reference baseline — Shen et al., Scientific Reports 9:12495 (2019), "Deep Learning to Improve Breast Cancer Detection on Screening Mammography"
Recipe: train a patch classifier on ROI crops (ResNet50 / VGG16, ImageNet-pretrained), then convert it into a whole-image classifier — end-to-end, no lesion annotation needed at the second stage.
CBIS-DDSM per-image AUC = 0.88 single model, 0.91 with 4-model averaging (sensitivity 86.1%, specificity 80.1%). On INbreast FFDM: AUC 0.95 → 0.98 (sensitivity 86.7%, specificity 96.1%).
This is a classification benchmark. There is no equally canonical segmentation benchmark on CBIS-DDSM — which is exactly the gap this project sits in.
works on ROI crops with a
SAM / SAM-2, box or point prompts
prompt = bounding box from the CSV

Shared training levers, whichever architecture wins: ImageNet transfer · patch pre-training (the Shen recipe) · aggressive augmentation (flip, elastic, intensity) · Dice+BCE, Tversky or focal loss to survive the 1:100+ foreground imbalance.

Sources — Lee R.S., Gimenez F., Hoogi A., Miyake K.K., Gorovoy M., Rubin D.L., "A curated mammography data set for use in computer-aided detection and diagnosis research", Scientific Data 4:170177 (2017), DOI 10.1038/sdata.2017.177 (local: sdata2017177.pdf).

TCIA collection record for CBIS-DDSM (1,566 participants · 2,620 studies · 6,775 series · 10,239 images · 163.51 GB · CC BY 3.0). Shen L. et al., Scientific Reports 9:12495 (2019), DOI 10.1038/s41598-019-48995-4. Kaggle mirror: awsaf49/cbis-ddsm-breast-cancer-image-dataset.
Grading criteria in the PIPELINE step 7 box are taken from Evaluation.pdf (MLB assessment grid) in this project folder. Project status as of 2026-09-08: dataset not yet downloaded, no code written.
